analysis:
The change is documentation only, in docs/operations/provider-release.md. It updates the prepared release from 0.10.9 to 0.10.10. It adds a mention of `darkbloom waitlist` and first-setup approval gates for Sandbox and cluster (#1742/#1850), and it rewrites the pre-tag checklist and rollout steps. I read all three units: the patch and the base text for lines 1-916. The base-text units show surrounding context only; the patch covers the changed hunks.

No code, workflow, signing, attestation or authorization logic changes in this diff. The checklist keeps the security-relevant release controls. It still requires toolchain Xcode 27.2 / SDK 27.2 / Swift 6.4.2, `check-date-comparisons.py`, `check-provider-weak-imports.py`, and the MLX submodule pins. It keeps the expected metallib_hash and the read-only cluster runtime facts dry run on the exact tag tree. It also keeps the requirement that the tagged commit is on verified master.

The new text says the 0.10.10 catalog room drops v0.10.8 cluster approvals. Pairs still on 0.10.8 then stop serving through Darkbloom. This is an availability and rollout note with a documented owner decision, not a regression. It touches A-018 and A-017 only operationally.

The diff drops the prior explicit sign-off sentence about checking that no pair on the omitted release serves. It also drops the platform-evidence table and the older enablement steps for GLM cache-routing allowlist and logprobs. These are doc-hygiene points, not security regressions. The text says the waitlist routes (darkbloom-platform #627) are independent and that first setups proceed as in 0.10.9 without them. The waitlist and first-setup gating code is not in this batch.

Open question for integration: the waitlist and approval gates in the feature PR #1850 introduce new attack surface in the CLI-to-coordinator path. It was not supplied and needs separate review. TB-013 and TB-014 may be affected.
